observations: Predicted more than twice as much wheat purchasable in1810 despite price rising2.4×; wage growth was not visible before answering.
Playfair view added weekly wage5→30 shillings,6×. Ratio view gave0.12→0.30 quarters,2.5×.
Marked best1785 at0.55 and worst1595 at0.09, demonstrating nonmonotonic progress.
Reveal accurately explained wage/price ratio and the limitation of one trade and one food versus a full cost of living.

complexity.reason: Requires interpreting ratios and different units.

whyCool: Dividing two familiar lines reveals a story that rising prices alone conceal.
caveat: Historical figures are one source, trade and food; exact wage growth is withheld until after the prediction.
effort: Completed prediction, nominal/ratio views, best/worst years, screenshots and reveal.
bucketReason: Strong transferable chart-reading lesson with a weakly informed initial estimate.

prediction.reason: Tests a historical prior, but wage information needed for the numerical conclusion is initially withheld.
prediction.evidence: Only price growth2.4× supplied before answering.

interaction.reason: Nominal series, ratio transformation and extrema reveal distinct aspects.
interaction.evidence: Dual-axis source view versus purchasing-power line.

payoff.reason: Correct ratio arithmetic and endpoint-versus-best distinction match observed values.

clarity.evidence: Quarters of wheat per weekly wage.

transfer.reason: A concrete data-reading method includes its applicability limit.
transfer.evidence: Divide wage by price; one food and trade not general living costs.

surprise.reason: Higher prices coexist with substantially higher purchasing power.
